# Where does the y-direction force come from in RNEA when the free flyer has both linear velocity and angular velocity in the z-direction?

> **Current answer:** The project contributor explicitly stated that [0,-1,0] is the Coriolis/Centrifugal effect, which can be calculated separately using pin.computeCoriolisMatrix(model, data, q, qd) @ qd. The free-flyer configuration should not be all-zero; using pin.neutral(model) ensures normalization of the quaternion. The contributor's use of the neutral configuration still reproduces the same cross-term, indicating it is not solely caused by a full-zero q. The original post did not respond to the question about whether the cross-term disappears after replacing q=0 with the neutral configuration. The answer is therefore a partial explanation.

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does RNEA return a y=-1 force when the free flyer has both z-direction linear velocity and x-direction angular velocity?
- When qd=[0,0,1,1,0,0] and qdd=0, RNEA returns [0,-1,9.81,0,0,0]; no y=-1 term is present when there is no speed or only z-direction linear velocity.
- When the x-direction angular velocity is replaced with an additional rotational joint speed, the cross-term disappears in the original author's supplementary example.

## Environment

- Pinocchio Python API, buildModelFromUrdf(..., JointModelFreeFlyer()), 1 kg point mass model; version, operating system, and hardware not specified.

## Priority diagnostics

- The project contributor stated that the [0,-1,0] can be calculated separately using pin.computeCoriolisMatrix(model, data, q, qd) @ qd, and compared with the RNEA extra term.
- Using pin.neutral(model) to initialize the free-flyer configuration prevents full-zero quaternions from being unnormalized.

## Possible causes

- The project contributor explicitly stated that [0,-1,0] is the Coriolis/Centrifugal effect.

## Attempts

- The original author used three sets of qd outputs to identify the bias term, and an additional rotational degree of freedom model was used for supplementary comparison.
- The project contributor replaced q=0 in the original code with pin.neutral(model), and reproduced the same y=-1 output.

## Effective fixes

- This is not a numerical error to be deleted; the term is identified as Coriolis/centrifugal speed bias, and pin.neutral(model) is used to initialize the valid free-flyer configuration.

## Result

- The project contributor provided a classification of the cross-term and a path for separate calculation, and used the neutral configuration to reproduce the original output.
